_readme: Vidrow Edit Kit format presets, transcribed from the Google Doc 'Vidrow Edit guidelines' (Format-wise Guidelines + Tool settings tables). Edit values freely; keep the keys. pause_cut_seconds: null means pause cutting is Off for that format (pauses are kept unless Claude marks them for removal). punch_ins.scales: the two framings alternated across jump cuts (1.0 = 100%). Ranges are seconds. 'guidance' is sent to Claude word for word.

formats.name: Podcast
formats.screen_coverage: Minimal, but never more than 3-4 s without a graphic

music.notes: Curious/suspense music. Very light bed (-22 dB or lower) in the Body only if the client wants it; no music under the hook. Risers for impact on hooks. No corporate music after the app is introduced.

punch_ins.notes: Doc has no tool-settings table for Podcast; bridge jumps with wide/reaction shots first, light punch-ins otherwise.

formats.guidance:
A clipped moment from a seated conversation that feels like the best 30 seconds of a long episode. Two or more people in a podcast setup (mics, seated, often multi-cam); the product or offer comes up naturally, usually voiced by the host or the guest expert.
Footage: opening shot shows the reaction shot of the host in split screen (for at least 3-4 seconds); clean lav or podcast-mic audio per speaker; optional cutaway reactions (nods, laughs, surprise).
Structure: Hook 2-5s = the most provocative or surprising line, cold-open, mid-sentence if needed. Body 20-40s = question -> expert answer -> the product/offer as the answer or proof -> one supporting point. CTA 2-4s = host or guest says the CTA naturally; end card with logo/offer.
Pacing: always cut to whoever is speaking; use the wide shot and reaction shots to bridge jumps if necessary. Trim every umm, false start and cross-talk; pauses under 0.4s. Keep 1 reaction shot in split screen every 6-10s so it feels like a conversation. Average shot length 2-3s.
Framing: only show the speaker/host from waist up. Active speaker full screen (9:16 crop of their close-up). Two speakers trading fast: stacked layout (one on top, one bottom) for that exchange. Keep eyes in the upper third; leave room for captions at the bottom.
Screens/graphics: minimal, but the video must not stay without graphics for more than 3-4 seconds; full-screen graphics allowed. Use a centred card so the speaker stays visible. Podcast branding (show name / logo bug) small in a corner after the client uses it.
Text: bold word-by-word captions, 2-4 words per line; speaker name + title lower third the first time each person appears; optional episode-style title card in the first second.
Music & sound: dialogue is king (voices peak around -6 dB), no music under the hook. Very light bed (-22 dB or lower) in the Body only if the client wants it. Subtle whoosh on hard layout changes. Use curious/suspense music. Avoid corporate-style music after the app is introduced. Risers for impact on hooks.
Avoid: cutting mid-word when switching speakers; long setups before the point; heavy graphics that kill the real-conversation feel.

formats.name: Gyan Pelo

music.notes: No music or SFX of any kind (music picked in the Music tab is still added).

formats.guidance:
Two people are seated, looking off-camera as if speaking to someone. The person in the foreground explains the product, while the person in the background listens and agrees.
Pacing: fast, jump cuts every 1.5-2.5s, no dead air (pauses under 0.3s).
Framing: both people visible in the frame, but no empty space in the direction the creator is looking; it must not feel as if the person is speaking to empty space. Screens in split screen for step-by-step app walkthroughs.
Screens/graphics/music: no graphics. No music or SFX of any kind. Only captions, screenshots and endslate.

formats.name: Skit
formats.tagline: Scripted mini-story, product is the turn
formats.screens: Minimal and split screen unless a green screen is on the phone; then full screen

music.notes: Music that matches the mood, never corporate. After the product is introduced switch to a different track of the same genre/feel (comedic -> another comedic track; emotional -> strings, then wholesome Indian-style after the app). Comedic SFX/stings sparingly on punchlines; reaction shots layered with funny SFX.

punch_ins.notes: Off; use reaction shots or zoom in/out punches to avoid abrupt jump cuts.

formats.guidance:
A scripted mini-story with characters, a problem and a payoff, where the product is the turning point. Usually comedic or relatable, two or more characters, sometimes a couple of locations. The conflict sets up the problem; the product resolves it; the ending lands a punchline or reaction.
Footage: wide/master, singles for each character, inserts of the product/phone; multiple takes per line; separate product shots and phone-screen recordings.
Structure: Hook 2-4s = drop straight into the conflict (in medias res), the funniest or most tense moment. Body 25-45s = setup -> problem escalates -> product moment (shown clearly) -> resolution / punchline. CTA 2-4s = character or VO delivers CTA; end card.
Hooks: three genuinely different angles that each set up the first Body line and never repeat it: the punchline or peak conflict line out of context; a visual gag or reaction shot that makes people ask what happened; a relatable POV situation text over the opening frame.
Pacing: respect comic and dramatic timing: do NOT cut pauses before a punchline or reaction. Use reaction shots or zoom in/out punches to avoid abrupt jump cuts. Shot-reverse-shot for dialogue; cut on action between angles. Pick takes for performance first, then continuity (props, positions, eyelines). Average shot length 1.5-3s.
Framing: the opening shot is always the master shot to establish the scene. Full-frame cinematic coverage, cropped to 9:16 with faces centred. Inserts (phone screen, product) full screen when the product is the hero. No split layouts unless the script calls for it (e.g. phone-call split).
Screens/graphics: skits always have a callout (yellow text under the script number); if none is in the script, add an editor to-do so the Post Production Manager provides one. Phone/app screens as split-screen/full-screen inserts at the product moment. Product hero shot if present in assets. No other graphics.
Text: dialogue captions on all spoken lines; POV or situation callout text only in the opening for 5-10 seconds.
Music & sound: mood-matching music, never corporate; switch to a different track of the same genre after the product is introduced. Emotional skits: strings rather than piano, then wholesome Indian-style after the app. Comedic SFX/stings sparingly on punchlines; reaction shots layered with funny SFX.

formats.name: Talking Head / Direct to camera

music.notes: Light trending curious music or library track under the Body (-20 dB), not under the first line of the hook. Curious-style music after the app is introduced. Pops on text/screen reveals, risers for suspense.

formats.guidance:
One creator, straight to camera, native UGC feel: fast, personal and persuasive. A single creator or actor speaking directly to the viewer, selfie-style or on a tripod: honest recommendation, problem-solution, or personal story with the product as the answer.
Footage: creator direct-to-camera with multiple takes per line; app screen recordings, product shots, offer screens; optional B-roll of the creator using the product.
Hooks: three genuinely different angles that each set up the first Body line and never repeat it, e.g. pain-point question (Kya aap bhi...?), bold claim or result (Maine 30 din mein...), pattern interrupt (unexpected statement, prop or location).
Pacing: jump cuts, no dead air (pauses under 0.3s). Best clean take per line (usually the last one). Alternate punch-ins (1.0 / 1.12) to hide jump cuts. Average shot length 1.5-2.5s.
Framing: face full screen most of the time. Screens as short cutaways (full screen 1-2.5s) or split screen (top band) while the creator keeps talking. Picture-in-picture for an app demo while the creator reacts.
Screens/graphics: show the matching screen exactly when the feature, price, offer or app name is said. 30-50% of the Body under screens for app clients; less for D2C. Logo / end card over the last 2s.
Text: bold captions throughout; offer, price and code as big text callouts; keep text inside Reels safe zones (avoid top 15% and bottom 20%). Roto of the subject is optional (editor to-do).
Music & sound: light trending curious music or library track under the Body (-20 dB), not under the first line of the hook. Subtle pops on text/screen reveals and risers for suspense. Curious-style music after the app is introduced.
Avoid: retakes or stumbles left in; screens that cover the face during emotional lines; generic stock B-roll that doesn't match what's said; corporate-style music.

formats.name: Street Interview
formats.tagline: One real conversation on the street

music.notes: No music; keep street ambience, it sells authenticity (music picked in the Music tab is still added).

punch_ins.notes: Doc pacing section says no punch-in zooms (abrupt cuts are fine); its tool table says 'On, light (1.0 / 1.08)'. Set enabled to true to use the light punch-ins.

formats.guidance:
A person talking into a handheld mic (the person holding the mic is not visible, only their hand). The exchange runs a little longer than a vox pop with one person, building to a reveal, surprise or demo of the product.
Footage: handheld shot of the interviewee with the mic hand visible; clean mic audio for both; street ambience.
Hooks: three hooks delivered separately that each set up the first Body line and never repeat it.
Pacing: fast. No punch-in zooms; abrupt cuts are fine in this format. Average shot length 2-3s.
Framing: only the interviewee and the hand holding the mic should be visible.
Screens/graphics: app screens in split screen only; endslate.
Text: the question as a callout at the top during the hook if it is not in the script; captions.
Music & sound: keep street ambience; no music.

formats.name: Vox Pop
formats.tagline: Many people, same question, rapid montage

music.notes: Driving music bed that carries the montage (-18 to -20 dB under voices); cut on the beat where possible; ambience low and consistent.

formats.guidance:
Many different people answer the same question in a rapid montage, and the pattern makes the point. Quick answers from several members of the public (or actors) to one question; the power comes from repetition, variety and contrast, ending on the product as the answer.
Footage: many short answers (2-3 people), each framed similarly; the same question asked the same way each time; optional final answer from a product user, plus product shots.
Hooks: three genuinely different angles that each set up the first Body line and never repeat it: rapid no / no idea / no montage on a simple question; one shocking answer then cut to black with the question; the question itself as a bold statement on screen.
Pacing: very fast, 1-2s per answer, cut on the answer, never on the setup. Group answers into a clear pattern; order for escalation and comedy. Remove the question audio after the first time (keep it as text). Pauses under 0.3s inside each answer.
Framing: each person full screen, faces at a consistent size and height across cuts; match colour/exposure; product reveal full screen.
Screens/graphics: callout if mentioned; medium graphics in split screen; app screens in split screen; end card with offer.
Text: callout if mentioned in the script; short captions per answer, highlight the key word.
Music & sound: driving music bed that carries the montage (-18 to -20 dB under voices); cut on the beat where possible; ambience low and consistent.
Avoid: answers that run long; inconsistent framing that makes the montage feel messy.
